newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY UNION-FITZPATRICK IMPROVING FOR BLEDISLOE.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-FITZPATRICK IMPROVING FOR BLEDISLOE.

text.p: Sean Fitzpatrick's injured knee has improved to the point where he is now a 50-50 chance of leading New Zealand in Saturday's Bledisloe Cup match against Australia, All Blacks coach John Hart announced on Friday.

Hart said the New Zealand captain successfully completed a private two-hour training session on Thursday night and would face a final fitness test on Saturday morning to determine whether he would play.

Fitzpatrick aggravated a knee injury during last week's epic 35-32 victory over South Africa in Johannesburg and was given little hope of playing in Saturday's match at the Melbourne Cricket Ground when the squad arrived in Australia on Tuesday.
"He never ceases to amaze me," Hart told a press conference on Friday. "Clearly there is still a bit of a problem but it has improved a lot and I'd say he's now a 50-50 chance."
Hart said that if Fitzpartick was ruled out, Auckland's Norm Hewitt would come into the team as the new hooker and Zinzan Brooke would take over the captaincy.
Australia skipper John Eales, meanwhile, defended his team against accusations that they were overawed by the All Blacks.
Eales said the Wallabies had beaten every other major power in world rugby during the past two seasons but hadn't been given enough recognition because of their failure to beat New Zealand.
"The All Blacks are the only team we haven't beaten since the start of last year and we have to. They are the benchmark," Eales said.
"I don't want to come across as though I'm whingeing but we have beaten teams this year that, while they're not as good as New Zealand, are up on the world stage," he said.
"We're not intimidated by them. We're looking forward to it, and there's no problems getting the guys up for this game."
A crowd of 100,000 is expected to attend Saturday's match which has been billed as one of the most eagerley-awaited Bledisloe Cup fixtures in years.
